title: 同朋友整湯圓慶祝冬至
scenario: Two friends discussing making tang yuan (glutinous rice balls) together to celebrate Winter Solstice (A1)

sourceNotes: The verb 整 (zing2) means "to make/prepare" and is commonly used in Cantonese for cooking and crafts, whereas Mandarin typically uses 做 (zou6). Both are correct but 整 is more colloquial in Hong Kong. The comparison pattern 好似...咁 (hou2 ci5...gam3) means "like/as...as": 好似耳仔咁軟 (hou2 ci5 ji5 zai2 gam3 jyun5) = "soft like an earlobe." This is a standard comparative structure. Reduplication of classifiers indicates plurality: 粒粒 (nap1 nap1) = "small balls (plural)." This is a common grammatical feature in Cantonese that adds a distributive or plural sense. The pattern 定 (ding6) in A-or-B questions: 自己整定買 (zi6 gei2 zing2 ding6 maai5) = "make yourself or buy?" This conjunction presents two alternatives for the listener to choose between. 左右 (zo2 jau6) means "approximately" and follows time expressions: 五分鐘左右 (ng5 fan1 zung1 zo2 jau6) = "about five minutes." Confidence Level: High
